readme.text: a slack bot that guards a channel.

someone joins the welcome channel
  └─▶ bot posts a welcome message + [ Fill in entry form ] button
        └─▶ applicant opens the form: name, how they found you, why they want in,
            then the Channel Confidentiality Agreement: tick "I agree to be bound by it" + type full name
              ├─ not signed ─▶ form won't submit (they can just cancel)
              └─ signed     ─▶ logged to PROMISES_FILE + a copy DMed to them
                                 OWNER_SLACK_ID set?  ─▶ DMed to you with Approve / Deny
                                 not set?             ─▶ auto-approved

a full written contract in the entry form, the Channel Confidentiality Agreement: parties, definitions of what's confidential, obligations (no screenshots, forwarding, retelling, posting, AI tools), permitted sharing of clearly non-sensitive stuff using common sense, exceptions, consideration (channel access), breach (permanent removal), duration, changes, and signature. applicants tick "I agree to be bound" and type their full name. wording lives in PROMISE_POINTS in src/agreement.ts; bump PROMISE_VERSION when you change it.

each promise is one JSON line in PROMISES_FILE (default data/promises.jsonl): slack user and team id, the name they gave, the full name they signed with, when, and the exact text they agreed to. if it can't be saved they aren't let in.

readme.text: A Command Code mod that shows throughput and latency while the agent works:
live tokens/second — an estimate (~) from streamed characters, refreshed while a request runs
time to first token (TTFT) — request start to the first observable generated content (text, reasoning, or a tool call)
last request — provider-reported output tokens over request wall time, including TTFT
session and lifetime averages — token-weighted throughput and mean TTFT
The widget sits above the prompt. /token-stats prints the full report, including per-model breakdowns.
From npm (also consumed by pnpm, which uses the npm registry):
Or copy this folder to ~/.commandcode/mods/token-metrics/ and let the user-mod scan pick it up. Send /reload after changing the source.

/token-stats reset session      clear this session, keep lifetime
/token-stats reset all          clear both (asks for confirmation)

readme.text: relay is a three-tier coding agent written in Rust. It separates thinking, editing and verification so that a model never grades its own work.
Tier 1 — planner (read-only). Inspects the repository with list_files,
read_file and search, then returns a structured plan. It has no write, shell or network tools.
Tier 2 — executor (staged workspace). A native Rust model/tool loop edits
an isolated copy of the repository through hash-checked patches. It cannot run shell commands or reach the original checkout.
Tier 3 — evaluator (Docker). Runs the approved test argv inside a
hardened container against a fresh copy of the staged snapshot. The verdict is deterministic process exit status, not a model opinion.
The harness owns approvals, budgets, sessions, evidence and the final apply. It supports local Ollama and hosted OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
Rust 1.88 or newer (edition 2024; let-chains are used).
For evaluation: Docker (or a compatible runtime), a running daemon, and the
For local models: Ollama running at http://localhost:11434.
Hosted providers need valid credentials and may charge money. There is no payment bypass, and no provider is contacted without a configured key.

readme.text: Launchly deploys vanilla static websites from public Git repositories.
public Git repository → clone → check root index.html → run Nginx → health check → live

It does not run repository build scripts and does not support Node, Python, Rust, Dockerfiles, or arbitrary application servers. A deployable repository simply contains index.html at its root, plus any HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, or fonts it needs.
Inspect the actual files and require root index.html.
Run the site with Podman using resource and privilege limits.
Require HTTP 200 on port 8080 before reporting live.
No generated Containerfiles, site image builds, Gemini calls, or repository commands are involved.
Fedora uses native Podman; do not use podman machine.

sudo dnf install -y git podman curl
sudo systemctl enable --now podman.socket

git clone https://github.com/gnahiak2/launchly.git
cd launchly
sudo mkdir -p /tmp/launchly
sudo chmod 777 /tmp/launchly
